question: A grocer purchased 50 kg of rice at ₹40 per kg and 20 kg of another variety of rice at ₹55 per kg. He mixed the two varieties and sold the entire mixture at ₹48 per kg. Find his total profit or loss in this transaction.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the profit or loss per kg for each variety relative to the selling price.

Profit on 50 kg rice = (48 − 40) × 50 = +8 × 50 = +₹400

Loss on 20 kg rice = (48 − 55) × 20 = −7 × 20 = −₹140

Net Profit = 400 − 140 = ₹260

**∴ The correct answer is Profit of ₹260.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Quantity 1 = 50 kg, Rate 1 = ₹40/kg

Quantity 2 = 20 kg, Rate 2 = ₹55/kg

Selling rate of mixture = ₹48/kg

**Formula Used:**

Total CP = (Q₁ × R₁) + (Q₂ × R₂)

Profit = Total SP − Total CP

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 50 kg @ ₹40
 CP: ₹2000

 CP: ₹1100

 Total CP
 ₹3100

 SP: ₹3360

 
• 
 
 Profit = SP − CP = 3360 − 3100 = ₹260

**Calculations:**

⇒ Cost Price of 50 kg of rice = 50 × 40 = ₹2000

⇒ Cost Price of 20 kg of rice = 20 × 55 = ₹1100

⇒ Total Cost Price (CP) = 2000 + 1100 = ₹3100

⇒ Total quantity of mixture = 50 + 20 = 70 kg

⇒ Total Selling Price (SP) of the mixture = 70 × 48 = ₹3360

⇒ Since SP > CP, there is a profit.

⇒ Profit = Total SP − Total CP = 3360 − 3100 = ₹260

**∴ The correct answer is Profit of ₹260.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basic Formula

Profit occurs when Selling Price > Cost Price. Profit = SP − CP.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Weighted Average Concept

Average Cost Price per unit of a mixture is calculated as (Q₁ × C₁ + Q₂ × C₂) ÷ (Q₁ + Q₂).
